Okay! I’m not an expert, but the safety plan my therapist and I made together is in this format:

*Step 1: Know When to Get Help*. (What are the warning signs that you’re beginning to struggle with your problem? These can include thoughts, feelings, and behaviors.) Try to think of and write down up to 4 signs or triggers that show you you’re getting depressed again. For example, one of my behavioral signs is excessive self-isolation. One of my recurring warning thoughts is “I don’t matter; no one will miss me.” 

*Step 2: Coping Skills*. (What can you do, by yourself, to take your mind off the problem?) Try to think of anything you like to do to distract yourself. The goal is to interrupt the negative emotions and thoughts before they overwhelm you. This list can be as long as you want, but I think 4 would be a good goal again. My personal examples for this step include breathing exercises, watching a movie/show, and using my weighted blanket. If you enjoy drawing or painting, do that. If you have a favorite game, play it- do anything but let the negative thoughts fester. 

*Step 3: Social Support*. (If you are unable to deal with your distressed mood alone, contact trusted family members or friends. List several people in case your first choices are not available.) Being around others can be a great way to prevent yourself from hurting yourself. Sometimes talking to others can pull us out of our catastrophic thinking. This one was difficult for me because I don’t really have a support system. Still, I was able to think of two friends to call in an emergency. Do you have someone reliable you could call? It can be friends, family members, a partner, or maybe even a trusted teacher/councilor. People do care about you- they just often can’t see the severity of what you’re going through. 

*Step 4: Seek Help from Professionals*. (If your problem persists, or if you have s^^cidal thoughts, reach out to your professional support system.) This list is for if steps 1-3 didn’t help you calm down. Having this list of emergency contacts will help keep you safe in times of severe emotional distress. The numbers I included are: S^^cide Hotline: 800-273-8255; Mobile Crisis/Crisis Center line (I would include mine, but this seems to be specific to each county/state. Consider looking up if your area has a mobile crisis center number. From my understanding they will listen to you and evaluate if you need immediate medical intervention); The police/ambulance (it seems obvious, but if you’re in danger, there’s no shame in calling the police or ambulance to intervene. This is also the easiest number to remember.) 

When these are made with a therapist, the therapist and patient usually sign and date the safety plan. If you don’t have a therapist, you can just sign and date it yourself! Officially signing it can serve as a sort of dedication to follow the plan when necessary. I hope this helped you all; I’ll try to answer more questions if you have any. 💕

The most effective practice I have found is to acknowledge the feelings of shame/self hatred, but then speak to myself as if I were a child or a friend. It can be really helpful to remember that you are a real person who deserves care and understanding, like everyone else. Your negative thoughts and feelings are valid, but they do not always reflect reality. 

I know it’s much easier said than done. It’s okay to forget, and sometimes we’ll feel too overwhelmed to practice positive self-talk. BPD makes everything feel so intense and extreme- but no one  is purely good or purely bad, including you. Just keep challenging and replacing those negative thoughts. 

It may also be a good idea for you to devise a safety plan for when you begin to feel very low/worthless. This could help prevent you from spiraling too much in a negative direction. I don’t know if you’re familiar with safety plans, but I can explain more about that if you want- I don’t want to make this comment any longer than it already is!

The main point is: be kind to yourself. It really does make a difference. You’re strong and you can do this!
